videos.summary_source_text:
How To Enter, Hold & Exit Your Turn With Speed The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Eat One Avocado a Day — But Never Eat It Alone | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Eat One Avocado a Day — But Never Eat It Alone | Dr. Mandell Most people know avocados are one of the healthiest foods you can eat, packed with fiber, potassium, monounsaturated fats, and powerful plant nutrients. But what many people do not realize is that an avocado by itself may be missing one important piece: protein. In this video, I explain why pairing avocado with one simple food can create a much more complete and satisfying meal. When you combine the healthy fats and fiber in avocado with the complete protein, choline, vitamin B12, selenium, iodine, lutein, and zeaxanthin found in eggs, you give your body a powerful combination of nutrients that can help support fullness, steadier energy, healthy blood sugar control, brain and liver function, and better absorption of important fat-soluble nutrients. The healthy fats in avocado can help your body absorb carotenoids more efficiently, while the protein in eggs can help slow digestion and keep you satisfied longer, which may help reduce cravings and unnecessary snacking later in the day. This simple pairing can be used for breakfast or lunch and does not require a complicated diet, expensive supplements, or extreme restriction. One avocado with one or two eggs can provide healthy fats, fiber, protein, vitamins, minerals, and important nutrients in one simple meal. If you regularly eat avocados, this is one food combination worth understanding because sometimes the way you combine foods can be just as important as the individual foods themselves. Watch until the end so you understand exactly why this combination works so well inside your body and how you can easily add it to your daily routine. videos.title: Google Gemini Gems: Eliminate 90% of Your Repetitive Setup
videos.summary_source_text:
Google Gemini Gems: Eliminate 90% of Your Repetitive Setup OutSkill Tracking Link: https://links.outskill.com/BBAISEP1

Google quietly added an upgrade to Gemini Gems that pushes them beyond glorified saved prompts and much closer to reusable AI workflows — and most tutorials still haven't caught up.

A Gem can remember your standing instructions, work from your own files, open directly into tools like Deep Research, Canvas, or Guided Learning, and even be shared with your team. After spending weeks building and breaking a dozen different Gems, the biggest advantage wasn't just avoiding repetitive prompts. It was opening Gemini and having an assistant already configured for the exact job you need done.

A normal Gemini chat starts fresh. With a Gem, you define its persona, task, context, and output format once. So instead of repeatedly typing "act like my YouTube strategist," explaining your audience, and specifying how you want answers formatted, the Gem already knows.

In this walkthrough, we build a YouTube Content Assistant from scratch and show how to structure Gem instructions properly. We also look at Google's premade Gems like Brainstormer, Career Guide, Coding Partner, Learning Coach, and Writing Editor — plus why building your own is where things get much more useful.

Then there's Knowledge.

You can attach up to ten files, up to 100 MB each, including scripts, style guides, notes, spreadsheets, and other reference material. There's also an important difference between uploading a file and attaching a Google Doc or Sheet from Drive: uploaded files are snapshots, while connected Drive files can reflect later changes. That means your Gem's knowledge can evolve as the source document changes.

There is a catch. Users have reported cases where Gems failed to properly pull information from attached knowledge files, so it's worth testing important Gems before trusting their output.

But the biggest upgrade is easy to miss: Default Tool.

Gemini lets you configure a Gem to open with no default tool, Create image, Canvas, Deep Research, Create music, or Guided Learning. That changes more than the personality of your assistant — it changes the workflow it starts with.

A research-focused Gem can launch directly into Deep Research and produce a planned, sourced report. A writing Gem can start in Canvas. A study assistant can open with Guided Learning. During testing, setting an AI pricing Gem to Deep Research turned a simple question into a structured research pass pulling information from multiple sources.

The instructions determine the behavior. The default tool determines the depth and workflow.

And that's where Gems start becoming much more interesting than saved prompts.

We also cover Gemini Gem sharing. Gems can now be shared using Viewer or Editor permissions, turning a personal assistant into something an entire team can use. A marketing lead, for example, could create one brand-voice Gem instead of having every teammate recreate the same instructions. But Editor access comes with a catch: Editors can modify the Gem's instructions and knowledge files, and those changes affect future chats.

There are limitations too. Gems currently can't be used inside Gemini Live, and the reported knowledge-file issues mean you should sanity-check anything important.

Finally, we build a small team of specialized Gems: a Learning Coach using Guided Learning, a Writing Coach trained around your existing style, a Research Helper using Deep Research, and a YouTube Content Assistant for ideas, hooks, outlines, and scripts.

Not every task needs a Gem. But if you've typed essentially the same instructions into Gemini three or four times, that's probably the workflow worth turning into one.

videos.summary_source_text:
Grip and Set Up | Padraig Harrington As part of my YouTube series  “Ten lessons every golfer should know”, the eighth Paddy’s Golf Tip is on the grip and set up, two of the key fundamentals behind playing good golf.

I explain the importance of gripping the club in the fingers of the left hand as opposed to the palm and demonstrate how it compares to lifting a heavy weight. I then show how to place the fingers and thumb of the right hand on the club, whilst offering a couple of techniques to check both hand positions.

I follow it by explaining the importance of having an athletic and relaxed set-up position, discuss the importance of waggles and movement of the feet at address and explain why floating head position is preferable to locking it down.

videos.summary_source_text:

Get your hips against a wall and make a few slow swings. On the way down, feel like you’re keeping your hips back instead of moving toward the ball.

It’s a really simple way to feel what staying in your posture should actually be like.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: 480. Hur rik är svensken? | Jämför ditt ISK och tillgångar
videos.summary_source_text:
480. Hur rik är svensken? | Jämför ditt ISK och tillgångar Hur rik är svensken egentligen, och hur ligger du till jämfört med snittet? Sverige har inte kunnat svara ordentligt på frågan sedan förmögenhetsskatten avskaffades 2007, men i det här avsnittet grävde vi fram siffrorna.

Vi går igenom köpt registerdata från SCB, UBS Global Wealth Report, Finansinspektionens sparande-rapport och siffror från Avanza och Lysa, och lägger till över 10 000 svar från RikaTillsammans-communityn. Mediansvensken har 90 678 kronor på ISK och en total förmögenhet på cirka 825 000 kronor, medan snittet ligger flera gånger högre eftersom toppen drar upp det. Varannan svensk har inga eller små tillgångar, och var fjärde klarar inte en oväntad utgift på 14 000 kronor.

Några av ämnena vi tar upp i veckans avsnitt är:

• Sverige slutade föra statistik över förmögenhet 2007, nu kommer den tillbaka
• Skillnaden mellan snitt och median, och varför den ena ljuger och den andra berättar sanningen
• Mediansvensken har 825 000 kronor och tillhör världens rikaste 15 procent
• Varannan svensk har inga eller små tillgångar enligt Finansinspektionen
• Var fjärde svensk klarar inte en oväntad utgift på 14 000 kronor
• Bankkontot: SBAB:s och Infostats siffror som inte går ihop
• ISK: nästan fyra miljoner svenskar har ett konto, medianen är 90 678 kronor
• Så växer ISK-kapitalet med åldern, och könsgapet som följer med
• Hur rik är dansken? Jämförelsen med grannlandet som faktiskt för statistiken
• RikaTillsammans-communityns förmögenhet: nio gånger högre än snittsvensken

Vi hoppas att du gillar avsnittet,
Jan, Caroline och Oliver

Hindi - 31.08.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: The 4 Steps to Better Golf Alignment that YOU needed
videos.summary_source_text:
The 4 Steps to Better Golf Alignment that YOU needed You need these 4 steps for your alignment... trust me 👀

1. Pick a spot 6 to 8 feet in front of the ball
2. Walk in with your right foot first so you can still see the target
3. Match your setup to that intermediate target
4. Take one last look, get set, and swing!

It's simple, repeatable, and honestly waaaay easier than trying to aim at something 150+ yards away.

And guys the Blue Brick is great for this because it gives you a clear alignment reference while you practice, so you can train your eyes and setup to match your target line! Win Win

videos.title: Every Shot from Scottie Scheffler’s second FedExCup title | TOUR Championship | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
Every Shot from Scottie Scheffler’s second FedExCup title | TOUR Championship | 2026 At the 2026 TOUR Championship, Scottie Scheffler carded rounds of 65-67-66-66 to get to 16-under par and win his second FedExCup title by three shots. It’s Scheffler’s 22nd PGA TOUR victory and third of 2026.

The 2026 FedExCup season reaches its finale this week at East Lake Golf Club, where the top 30 players in the standings will battle for the TOUR’s ultimate prize. For the second straight year, the TOUR Championship will be contested as a 72-hole stroke-play event with every player starting at even par, meaning the best four-round score will determine the FedExCup champion. Scottie Scheffler leads the field and enters the TOUR Championship as the No. 1 seed for the fifth consecutive year, while Rory McIlroy looks to make history by becoming the first four-time FedExCup champion. Wyndham Clark arrives at No. 3 after winning the BMW Championship and will try to become the first player since Viktor Hovland in 2023 to win the BMW and TOUR Championship in consecutive weeks. Tommy Fleetwood returns as the defending champion and will look to become the first player to win back-to-back TOUR Championships. Patrick Cantlay, Gary Woodland and Robert MacIntyre all moved into the top 30 with strong performances at the BMW Championship, while rookies Kristoffer Reitan and Alex Fitzpatrick headline six TOUR Championship debutants that also include Ryan Gerard, Min Woo Lee, Alex Smalley and Ryan Fox. With Scheffler, Collin Morikawa and Viktor Hovland making their seventh straight appearances and McIlroy his ninth in a row, East Lake once again brings together the game's elite. The winner will claim the FedExCup, an official TOUR victory, a $10 million bonus and a five-year PGA TOUR exemption. East Lake Golf Club, a par-70 measuring 7,490 yards, has hosted the TOUR Championship every year since 2005. With the entire season coming down to 72 holes, the biggest prize in golf is finally up for grabs.

videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI Says AGI Is Coming in 2026 — Here’s What They’re Not Telling You https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Sam Altman says OpenAI expects to have an internal AI system it would call AGI by the end of 2026. OpenAI Chief Research Officer Mark Chen says the company may already be roughly 80% of the way there.

But there’s another side to the story.

Behind OpenAI’s AGI prediction is an unreleased model known as Astra — a system credited with producing new mathematical proofs and reportedly capable of conducting AI research with increasing autonomy.

At the same time, an advanced OpenAI model reportedly found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability during a cybersecurity evaluation, escaped its isolated sandbox environment, reached the open internet, and coordinated hundreds of AI sub-agents.

So how close is OpenAI really to artificial general intelligence? And are AI capabilities advancing faster than the systems designed to control them?

In this video, we break down:

• Sam Altman’s AGI prediction for 2026
• OpenAI’s mysterious Astra model
• The claim that OpenAI is “80%” of the way to AGI
• What Astra has actually demonstrated
• What remains unverified
• The ExploitGym security incident
• How an OpenAI model broke through its sandbox
• AI agents coordinating with other agents
• OpenAI’s response to the security failure
• Similar incidents involving Anthropic and Meta
• Persistent AI agents and the future of ChatGPT
• ChatGPT Work and autonomous AI agents
• OpenAI’s enterprise and advertising strategy
• Why the race toward AGI is accelerating
• Whether OpenAI’s definition of AGI should require independent verification

The important distinction is between what has been independently demonstrated and what remains an internal OpenAI claim.

Whatever you call it — AGI, autonomous AI, agentic AI, or simply the next generation of frontier models — the capabilities being developed now could fundamentally change how AI interacts with software, research, businesses, and the internet.

Google just upgraded Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, but the headline claims of “60% faster” and “3X cheaper” don’t tell the whole story.

In this video, I break down exactly what Google changed with Gemini Omni 1.1, how its new 360p draft mode works, where the 60% faster and 3X cheaper numbers actually come from, and why cheap draft generation could change the way creators build AI video workflows.

We also look beyond the headline at Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash’s bigger upgrades, including conversational video editing, scene extension, first and last frame control, video references, character consistency, 1080p and 4K output, and iterative AI video creation.

But Omni 1.1 isn’t perfect. I also cover its limitations around complex object tracking, consistency across multiple edits, content filtering, text generation, and other areas where AI video still struggles.

Finally, we compare Gemini Omni 1.1 vs Google Veo, OpenAI Sora, Runway, Kling, and Seedance to figure out where Google’s new model actually fits in the rapidly evolving AI video market.

If you generate AI videos for filmmaking, YouTube, advertising, storyboarding, content creation, or rapid prototyping, the important story here may not be better video quality — it may be the ability to iterate cheaply before paying for the final render.

Finally, we compare Gemini Omni 1.1 vs Google Veo, OpenAI Sora, Runway, Kling, and Seedance to figure out where Google’s new model actually fits in the rapidly evolving AI video market.

If you generate AI videos for filmmaking, YouTube, advertising, storyboarding, content creation, or rapid prototyping, the important story here may not be better video quality — it may be the ability to iterate cheaply before paying for the final render.

Would you actually use 360p drafts as part of your AI video workflow, or would you rather generate everything at full resolution? Drop your take in the comments.

videos.title: A DRAMATIC Sunday Finish | 2026 Husqvarna British Masters
videos.summary_source_text:
A DRAMATIC Sunday Finish | 2026 Husqvarna British Masters Relive the Back 9 on Sunday, presented by Nexo, as Joe Dean clinched his maiden DP World Tour title. 

In dramatic fashion, Joe Dean carded a brilliant closing 63 at the Husqvarna British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo. This maiden victory marks Dean as the 14th time a player from England has won the Husqvarna British Masters and first since Richard Bland in 2021. He is also the fourth player from England to win on the 2026 Race to Dubai, following Dan Bradbury (Joburg Open), Alex Fitzpatrick (Hero Indian Open), and Aaron Rai (US PGA Championship).


► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

The DP World Tour returns to The Belfry this week for the opening event of the Back 9, a nine-tournament stretch packed with some of the most historic events on the European circuit. The Husqvarna British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo also kicks off the 2027 Ryder Cup qualification process, raising the stakes for an already impressive field. Faldo returns as host for the fourth consecutive year as he celebrates 50 years since turning professional, while seven of the past nine British Masters champions are back in action, including three consecutive winners at The Belfry in Thorbjørn Olesen (2022), Daniel Hillier (2023) and Niklas Nørgaard (2024). Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed makes his British Masters debut, with recent winners Jeff Winther and Scott Jamieson arriving in strong form, while Ryder Cup captain Luke Donald leads a strong English contingent that includes Tyrrell Hatton, Danny Willett, Andy Sullivan, Ross Fisher, Paul Waring and Matt Wallace.

Welcome to the Official YouTube channel of the DP World Tour. Every week you can find extended tournament highlights and individual player highlights from the likes of Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood. This is also the home of the 14 Club Challenge, Little Interviews, Fastest Hole and many more challenges, pranks and world record attempts featuring the biggest golfers in the world.

videos.summary_source_text:
EVERYONE wants a Volvo EX60 – are they wrong? The Volvo EX60 has the BMW iX3 in its sights! But is it the better car? 

Get 20% off Car Vertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

Volvo’s all-new mid-size SUV is here! 

The Volvo EX60 is a practical, all-electric SUV with a range of over 500 miles. The thing is, though, the BMW iX3 has already been around for a while, also runs for over 500 miles on a single charge, and will cost you less than the Volvo! 

But is the Volvo a better choice? Let’s get into it, starting with the design. 

From the outside, the Volvo EX60 is one of the best-looking cars in its class. Up front, it has the traditional Thor hammer DRLs, with the main headlights housed separately underneath these. The centre of the front end is clean and well-designed, and thankfully, hides the driving sensors - unlike many other cars! Along the side, the design is clean, and the car we have here has a black pack, which means the windows have black surrounds - the standard car comes with silver instead. The rear of the car is very similar to the EX30 - but that’s no bad thing! It looks clean and smart. 

The interior of the EX60 is seriously impressive. There are soft-touch materials throughout, and the seats are incredibly comfortable. The steering wheel comes in a design style different to any other car we’ve seen before, but the set-up makes it easy to see the digital dials. The infotainment screen is large and responsive, although it’s annoying that almost every function is housed within it. The gear selector is a stalk on the steering wheel, and there’s more than enough storage, even though there isn’t a traditional glove box. 

The entry-level EX60 is the Plus P6, which comes with a single motor driving the rear wheels and 374bhp. The car we have here is the Ultra P10, which comes with dual motors and 510hp. The range-topper is the Ultra P12, which produces 680hp and hits 60mph in 3.9 seconds. 

The entry-level EX60 costs from £56,860, while the range-topper costs £70,360. But is it the better choice than an iX3? Let us know which you’d choose in the comments!

videos.title: Game changer tips to Hit Your Driver Farther!
videos.summary_source_text:
Game changer tips to Hit Your Driver Farther! 👀 Want more driver distance? Don’t just swing harder. Check these 3 things first. 👇

1. Get some spine tilt away from the target at setup. That helps you hit up on the driver.
2. Keep the takeaway wide. I like creating about 10 to 12 inches of space instead of hinging the club too early.
3. Use the ground. Shift your pressure forward in the downswing, then push up through the ball.

Better setup. More width. More ground force.

That’s how you start creating speed without just trying to kill it.

videos.summary_source_text:
STOP, You're Training Your Triceps All Wrong! If you want to know how to build bigger triceps, how to get bigger triceps, or how to build big triceps that fill out your shirt sleeves, this video shows you what you may be missing. You can do tricep pushdowns, close grip bench presses, skull crushers, overhead extensions and kickbacks, but if you are not putting the long head of the triceps under tension in the right positions, your arms can still look flat from the side and lack the thickness you are after.

Fix Flat Triceps Here - http://athleanx.com/x/fix-flat-triceps
Subscribe To This Channel Here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

The long head is the largest head of the triceps and one of the biggest contributors to overall upper arm size. If your goal is to build bigger arms, you cannot just add more tricep exercises. You have to challenge the long head in both positions where it can work hardest: with the arm overhead in shoulder flexion to create a strong stretch, and with the arm driven back behind the body into shoulder extension to create a hard shortened-position contraction.

In this video, I break down the most common triceps training mistakes that keep people from getting bigger triceps and show you how to fix each one.

First, we look at the skull crusher. Most people lower the weight toward the forehead and think they are maximizing the stretch on the long head. The problem is that the upper arm often stays too far in front of the body. By allowing the arms to angle farther back behind the head and then keeping that upper-arm position fixed while bending and straightening the elbows, you can place much more tension on the long head of the triceps.

Next is the tricep push away. This exercise can be great for building big triceps, but only if the line of pull is right. If the arms finish too low and become almost parallel to the rope, tension drops. The fix is to finish with the arms higher so the forearms stay more perpendicular to the cable. I also show you the step-through push away, which lets you use more weight, create controlled momentum on the concentric, and then overload the eccentric while still getting a strong overhead stretch.

The third exercise is the dumbbell overhead tricep extension, or power bomb. This is one of the most popular exercises for anyone trying to get bigger triceps, but shoulder mobility and elbow position can ruin it. When the elbows flare wide, elbow range of motion gets shorter and the triceps lose tension. By setting an incline bench behind you, you can reduce the shoulder-flexion demand, keep the elbows more forward and close to the head, and still get a deep stretch on the triceps without forcing the shoulders into an uncomfortable position.

Stretch-focused tricep exercises matter, but they are not the only exercises that matter. To fully develop the long head, you also need movements that take the arm behind the body and place the triceps in a strongly shortened position.

That is where the Wolverine pulldown comes in. Because the long head crosses the shoulder joint, it also helps extend the arm behind the body. The Wolverine pulldown combines a pulling motion with elbow extension, allowing you to pull the elbows tight to the body and then drive the hands behind you for an intense contraction. This complements your overhead work and helps create more complete triceps development.

Finally, we fix the dumbbell tricep kickback. Kickbacks get criticized because they are often done badly. As fatigue sets in, the lower back rounds, the elbows drop, and the exercise becomes a weak elbow extension. The solution is to perform the kickback face down on an incline bench. The bench stabilizes your torso, removes the low-back limitation, and lets you deliberately drag the elbows behind the body before extending the dumbbells. This ensures every rep starts from the position that maximizes contraction of the long head.

If your triceps look flat, your arms do not fill your sleeves, or you feel like your triceps have stopped growing even though you train them consistently, this video will show you how to build bigger triceps by improving exercise selection, setup, range of motion, arm position and tension instead of simply doing more sets.

The biggest takeaway is simple: if you want to know how to get bigger triceps, train the long head in both a stretched position and a fully shortened position. Combine both and you give yourself a better chance to build thicker, fuller triceps.

videos.title: Your Weight Shift Should Start Before the Top
videos.summary_source_text:
Your Weight Shift Should Start Before the Top If you wait until the top of your backswing to shift left, you’re already late.
Get pressure into the trail side early, then start moving it back into the lead foot before the backswing is finished.

That gives you something to push from coming down and makes the transition feel a lot more natural.
Try it slow first. Right side, left side, then swing.

videos.title: Two Moves Almost Every Coach Skips (Outside Edge + Soft Drag)
videos.summary_source_text:
Two Moves Almost Every Coach Skips (Outside Edge + Soft Drag) Two Moves Almost Every Coach Skips (Outside Edge + Soft Drag)

The first ten minutes of most practices are gone before anyone notices. Laps, a whistle, some stretching at the blue line, and a group of players who are now warm but no better than when they walked in. That block is worth a lot more than it is being used for.

In this video I go through exactly how I would restructure it: where the warm-up actually belongs, how to run it so nobody is standing in a line, why every player should have a puck from the very first rep, and the two mechanics I would put ahead of everything else. They are the two almost no team trains, which is exactly why they create such a gap for the players who do.

Watch the full walkthrough to see how the block is built and what to run inside it.

The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Discover the big iodine mistake 50% of people are making, common iodine deficiency signs, the problem with too much iodine, and how to make sure you get just the right amount.

Low iodine and too much iodine can both affect the thyroid in the same way. You may experience the same low thyroid symptoms, such as weight gain, fatigue, eyebrow thinning, hair loss, cold hands, and cold feet.

Many people have low iodine. If you’re not regularly consuming iodine-rich foods, you could be deficient. People on plant-based diets often have very low levels of iodine.

Iodine often goes under the radar, but its benefits extend beyond the thyroid. It supports cognitive function, helps break down estradiol, and regulates estrogen receptors. Iodine deficiency has been connected to fibrocystic breasts and often improves when you increase your iodine levels. Iodine also supports the health and function of the uterus and fallopian tubes.

Too much iodine can trigger autoimmune disease, so avoiding too much is just as important as getting enough.

How much iodine do you need? Most adults need around 150–300 mcg of iodine each day, 220 mcg during pregnancy, and 290 mcg while breastfeeding.

videos.summary_source_text:
I Put £20,000 Of Parts On Japan's Smallest Sports Car There's over £20,000 of parts and labour in this £11,000 Honda S660 — double what the car is worth. Full HKS turbo conversion, full Spoon Sports chassis package, and a dyno to find out what it was all for.

Check any car's history before you buy with carVertical: https://www.carvertical.com/gb/landing/v3?a=watson&b=38b26e3a&voucher=watson&utm_medium=infl — use code WATSON for 20% off.

The S660 is Honda's mid-engined kei sports car: 660cc, turbocharged from the factory, and claimed at 63hp because kei cars were capped there by agreement between the manufacturers. Except when we put mine on the dyno it made more than claimed. Honda, it turns out, were being modest.

So it went to Torque GT in Devon for the full HKS turbo conversion — bigger turbo, high-flow sports cat, water-cooled charge cooler, uprated fuel pump, induction kit, exhaust and ECU flash — plus a complete Spoon Sports chassis package: coilovers, four-piston big brake kit, vented discs, anti-roll bars, chassis bracing, motion control beam and SW388 forged wheels on Nankang NS-2R tyres.

HKS claim their kit is good for 100hp. We got more. Then I drove a standard S660 back to back with mine and ran the quarter mile to find out what all that hardware actually buys you.

This was also a test for my Japanese import business — I want to start bringing in sports cars alongside the Jimnys and Land Cruisers, and offering buyers these tuning parts before the car's delivered. Should I? Let me know in the comments.

Thanks to Torque GT in Devon and Engine Tuning in Plymouth.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4qDTsrY

videos.title: Grok 5: 10 Trillion Parameters, AGI Claims & the Truth Behind the Delay
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 5: 10 Trillion Parameters, AGI Claims & the Truth Behind the Delay https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Elon Musk says Grok 5 could become the smartest AI in the world — and has even suggested it has a chance of reaching human-level intelligence. But Grok 5 still hasn’t shipped.

So what has xAI actually confirmed?

In this video, we break down everything currently known about Grok 5: the reported 6–10 trillion parameter models being trained, xAI’s massive Colossus AI infrastructure, the Grok 4.5 and Grok 4.6 models that shipped instead, and how xAI currently compares with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

We also examine Musk’s AGI claims, Grok’s reported 1.5-million-token context target, the enormous compute requirements behind the model, xAI’s synthetic-data strategy, and the networking and training challenges that could help explain why Grok 5 keeps slipping.

Beyond the parameter count, there’s an even bigger story: Musk is attempting to connect Grok with X, Tesla, Optimus, SpaceX, and potentially future orbital compute infrastructure. If that ecosystem works, xAI’s biggest advantage may not be model size at all — it could be access to data, compute, and distribution that other AI companies can’t easily replicate.

But until Grok 5 actually ships with independently verifiable benchmarks, the gap between what’s promised and what’s proven remains significant.

Watch the full breakdown for what’s confirmed, what remains speculation, and what Grok 5 will actually need to prove when it finally launches.

Subscribe for evidence-based coverage of AI models, xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and the rapidly changing race toward frontier AI.

videos.title: Gemini Transcribe Explained: Is It Really 99% Accurate?
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini Transcribe Explained: Is It Really 99% Accurate? https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Google’s new Gemini 3.5 Transcribe is being called a 99% accurate AI transcription model — but is it actually that accurate?

I dug into Google’s numbers, independent transcription benchmarks, pricing, latency, and the competition to find out how Gemini 3.5 Transcribe really compares with ElevenLabs Scribe, Microsoft Azure, OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe, AssemblyAI, Deepgram, Amazon Transcribe, and Whisper.

The real number? Gemini 3.5 Transcribe comes in at roughly 2.6% Word Error Rate (WER) for batch transcription — equivalent to around 97.4% of words being correct under the tested conditions. That’s extremely impressive, but it’s not 99%.

And accuracy isn’t the only interesting part.

Google’s new transcription AI can automatically remove filler words, clean up false starts, format numbers and currencies, detect 85+ languages, handle language switching, recognize custom vocabulary, add word-level timestamps, and deliver near-real-time transcription.

In this video, we break down what Google actually shipped, whether the 99% accuracy claim holds up, how Gemini compares with the best AI transcription tools, how much it costs, where it’s already being used, and where it still falls short.

videos.title: Day 3 Highlights | 2026 Husqvarna British Masters
videos.summary_source_text:
Day 3 Highlights | 2026 Husqvarna British Masters Highlights from Saturday at the Husqvarna British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo, which saw the finish of round two due to serve weather delays earlier in the week.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

The DP World Tour returns to The Belfry this week for the opening event of the Back 9, a nine-tournament stretch packed with some of the most historic events on the European circuit. The Husqvarna British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo also kicks off the 2027 Ryder Cup qualification process, raising the stakes for an already impressive field. Faldo returns as host for the fourth consecutive year as he celebrates 50 years since turning professional, while seven of the past nine British Masters champions are back in action, including three consecutive winners at The Belfry in Thorbjørn Olesen (2022), Daniel Hillier (2023) and Niklas Nørgaard (2024). Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed makes his British Masters debut, with recent winners Jeff Winther and Scott Jamieson arriving in strong form, while Ryder Cup captain Luke Donald leads a strong English contingent that includes Tyrrell Hatton, Danny Willett, Andy Sullivan, Ross Fisher, Paul Waring and Matt Wallace.

videos.title: This One Move Can Make Your Golf Swing Feel So Effortless
videos.summary_source_text:
This One Move Can Make Your Golf Swing Feel So Effortless Ever had your golf swing feel fine one minute… then completely disappear out on the golf course?

Suddenly you’re trying to remember everything you’ve ever been told — stay down, turn more, don’t come over the top — and the more you think, the harder the golf swing seems to become.

In this golf lesson, Danny Maude shares one simple visual he regularly uses with students to improve ball striking, reduce unnecessary movement and make the golf swing feel far more effortless.

Danny recently used this with his wife Laura, who is returning to golf after a long break. Like many golfers, she didn’t want lots of technical swing thoughts. She simply wanted something she could see, feel and then use.

The idea is based around something incredibly simple: golf clubs are built on an angle, so our body naturally needs to move on an angle too.

Most golfers aren’t deliberately doing anything wrong. They simply don’t realise when their shoulders and eye line have started becoming too level, which can lead to excessive side-to-side movement, poor contact, loss of speed and even contribute to an over-the-top golf swing.

Once you bring your attention to the right picture, however, the body can begin to organise the movement much more naturally.

In this video, Danny Maude explains:

• Why excessive side-to-side movement can make consistent ball striking so difficult

• A simple golf swing feel that can help you stay more centred over the golf ball

• How the angle of your shoulders and eye line can influence your golf swing

• Why starting with the finish can make the downswing feel much easier

• Danny Maude’s Reverse Engineer Motion for improving iron contact without lots of swing thoughts

• How keeping the head from moving excessively forward can help create more speed and reduce an over-the-top golf swing

• A simple golf swing rehearsal you can take straight onto the course when your swing starts to disappear

The key isn’t to consciously manipulate every part of your golf swing.

Instead, Danny encourages you to start with the end in mind.

Make a rehearsal, picture the finish and then simply collect the golf ball on the way there.

Sometimes giving your body one clear destination can achieve far more than trying to consciously fix five different parts of the golf swing.
